paragraphs.text: This area has 10 documented events, and some locations in this account are approximate.
Prochorus, born here at a date given only as 1 CE to 100 CE, was one of the Seven Deacons chosen to care for the poor of the Christian community in Jerusalem.
Josephus, best known for writing The Jewish War, was born in Jerusalem around 37 CE.
Around 48 to 50 CE came the Council of Jerusalem, the first Christian synod.
In 66 CE riots in Jerusalem became the catalyst of the First Jewish-Roman War, and the Battle of Jerusalem was fought.
In 67 CE, according to Josephus, the Sicarii of Masada raided Ein Gedi and killed 700 of its inhabitants.
In 68 CE came the Zealot Temple Siege and the Battle of the Jordan River.
In 70 CE Roman forces led by Titus besieged Jerusalem, destroyed the Second Temple, and razed the city, the effective end of the First Jewish Revolt.
The Siege of Machaerus followed in 71 CE, and from 72 CE to 73 CE Roman imperial forces took the hilltop fortress of Masada, held by the Sicarii.
Hegesippus, a Christian writer of the early Church, was born here in 107 CE, and the Siege of Betar is dated 132 CE to 135 CE.
